verses.english_translation: O Arjuna! Why give way to unmanliness? O thou, who art the terror of thy enemies! Shake off such shameful effeminacy and make ready to act!
verses.attribution: English translation • Shri Purohit Swami (1935, Public Domain)

verses.english_translation: My heart is oppressed with pity, and my mind is confused as to what my duty is. Therefore, my Lord, tell me what is best for my spiritual welfare, for I am Your disciple. Please direct me, I pray.
verses.attribution: English translation • Shri Purohit Swami (1935, Public Domain)

verses.english_translation: As the soul experiences infancy, youth, and old age in this body, so finally it passes into another, the wise have no delusion about this.
verses.attribution: English translation • Shri Purohit Swami (1935, Public Domain)

verses.english_translation: It was not born; it will never die, nor, once having been, can it cease to exist. Unborn, eternal, ever-enduring, yet most ancient, the spirit does not die when the body is dead.
verses.attribution: English translation • Shri Purohit Swami (1935, Public Domain)

verses.english_translation: As a man discards his threadbare robes and puts on new ones, so the Spirit throws off its worn-out bodies and takes on fresh ones.
verses.attribution: English translation • Shri Purohit Swami (1935, Public Domain)

verses.english_translation: Weapons cannot cleave it, fire cannot burn it, water cannot drench it, and wind cannot dry it.
verses.attribution: English translation • Shri Purohit Swami (1935, Public Domain)

verses.english_translation: But you have only the right to work, but none to the fruit of it. Let not the fruit of your action be your motive; nor be you enamored of inaction.
verses.attribution: English translation • Shri Purohit Swami (1935, Public Domain)

verses.english_translation: Perform all your actions with your mind concentrated on the Divine, renouncing attachment and looking upon success and failure with an equal eye. Spirituality implies equanimity.
verses.attribution: English translation • Shri Purohit Swami (1935, Public Domain)

verses.english_translation: When a person dwells on the objects of sense, they create an attraction for them; this attraction develops into desire, and desire breeds anger.
verses.attribution: English translation • Shri Purohit Swami (1935, Public Domain)

verses.english_translation: Anger induces delusion; delusion leads to loss of memory; loss of memory results in the shattering of reason; and the destruction of reason leads to destruction.
verses.attribution: English translation • Shri Purohit Swami (1935, Public Domain)

verses.english_translation: Do your duty as prescribed, for action for duty's sake is superior to inaction. Even the maintenance of the body would be impossible if one remained inactive.
verses.attribution: English translation • Shri Purohit Swami (1935, Public Domain)

verses.english_translation: Action is the product of the qualities inherent in nature. It is only the ignorant man who, misled by personal egotism, says, "I am the doer."
verses.attribution: English translation • Shri Purohit Swami (1935, Public Domain)

verses.english_translation: It is better to do one's own duty, however lacking in merit, than to do that of another, even though efficiently. It is better to die doing one's own duty, for doing the duty of another is fraught with danger.
verses.attribution: English translation • Shri Purohit Swami (1935, Public Domain)

verses.english_translation: Lord Shri Krishna: It is desire, it is aversion, born of passion. Desire consumes and corrupts all things. It is the greatest enemy of man.
verses.attribution: English translation • Shri Purohit Swami (1935, Public Domain)

verses.english_translation: Let him seek liberation with the help of his Highest Self, and never disgrace his own Self. For that Self is his only friend; yet it can also be his enemy.
verses.attribution: English translation • Shri Purohit Swami (1935, Public Domain)

verses.english_translation: When the volatile and wavering mind wanders, let him restrain it and bring it back to its allegiance to the Self.
verses.attribution: English translation • Shri Purohit Swami (1935, Public Domain)

verses.english_translation: He who sees Me in everything and everything in Me, I shall never forsake him, nor shall he lose Me.
verses.attribution: English translation • Shri Purohit Swami (1935, Public Domain)

verses.english_translation: O Arjuna! He is the perfect saint who, having been taught by the likeness within himself, sees the same Self everywhere, regardless of whether the outer form be pleasurable or painful.
verses.attribution: English translation • Shri Purohit Swami (1935, Public Domain)

verses.english_translation: My Lord! Verily, the mind is fickle and turbulent, obstinate, and strong; indeed, it is extremely difficult to control, like the wind.
verses.attribution: English translation • Shri Purohit Swami (1935, Public Domain)

verses.english_translation: Lord Shri Krishna replied: Doubtless, O Mighty One, the mind is fickle and exceedingly difficult to restrain; however, O Son of Kunti, with practice and renunciation, it can be done.
verses.attribution: English translation • Shri Purohit Swami (1935, Public Domain)

verses.english_translation: I am the same to all beings; I do not favour any, nor do I hate any. However, those who worship Me devotedly, they live in Me and I in them.
verses.attribution: English translation • Shri Purohit Swami (1935, Public Domain)

verses.english_translation: Then gird up your loins and conquer. Subdue your foes and enjoy the kingdom in prosperity. I have already doomed them. Be thou my instrument, Arjuna!
verses.attribution: English translation • Shri Purohit Swami (1935, Public Domain)

verses.english_translation: He who is incapable of hatred towards any being, who is kind and compassionate, free from selfishness, without pride, equable in pleasure and pain, and forgiving.
verses.attribution: English translation • Shri Purohit Swami (1935, Public Domain)

verses.english_translation: The gates of hell are three: lust, wrath, and avarice; they destroy the Self, so avoid them.
verses.attribution: English translation • Shri Purohit Swami (1935, Public Domain)

verses.english_translation: While the pleasure that drugs the senses from start to finish, which springs from indolence, lethargy, and folly—that pleasure flows from Ignorance.
verses.attribution: English translation • Shri Purohit Swami (1935, Public Domain)

verses.english_translation: It is better to do one's own duty, however defective it may be, than to follow the duty of another, however well one may perform it. He who does his duty as his own nature reveals it, never commits a sin.
verses.attribution: English translation • Shri Purohit Swami (1935, Public Domain)

verses.english_translation: Fix your mind on Me, and by My grace you will overcome the obstacles in your path. But if, misled by pride, you do not listen, then you will indeed be lost.
verses.attribution: English translation • Shri Purohit Swami (1935, Public Domain)

verses.english_translation: Give up your earthly duties, surrender yourself to Me alone. Do not be anxious; I will absolve you from all your sins.
verses.attribution: English translation • Shri Purohit Swami (1935, Public Domain)
